findings.claim: The design panel IS 1:1 with the repo. Under the real hython the live panel loads the MAIN tree (deployed package SYNAPSE_ROOT=C:/Users/User/SYNAPSE, master 22019f52); branch da6d2b33 == master on all 90 python/synapse/panel/**.py (git diff empty), and worktree bytes == loaded bytes for all 90 modules. The 'master da6d2b33' behavior anchor is therefore byte-equal to the code the panel runs.

The 'stale after relaunch' concern is DISPROVEN at the code/module layer. The pypanel flush provably evicts every synapse.* module and forces a fresh disk re-import on relaunch (module id changed across the flush; non-synapse control survived, so the flush is scoped, not a blanket nuke). A panel relaunch cannot serve a stale in-memory panel module.

HONEST SCOPE LIMIT (out of scope, Joe's seat): this proves the flush mechanism + code parity HEADLESS. It does NOT reproduce a live long-lived Houdini GUI session's actual panel close/reopen, and GUI pixel render is out of scope by mandate. If Joe still observes 'stale' from the live seat, it is NOT module divergence (disproven) and NOT a missing flush (disproven) — the next place to look is Houdini's own pane/panel-definition caching or a pinned pane that does not re-invoke onCreateInterface() on reopen.

findings.claim: Two-tree deployment reality (observation, non-blocking): the deployed package points the live panel at the MAIN tree, so panel edits made in a worktree are NOT what the live panel runs until merged to master. Relevant for any future panel-parity work that edits panel/ in a worktree and expects the running panel to reflect it.

Independently crucible-verified CONFIRMED-SOUND: denominator genuinely exhaustive (90==90 reproduced on both trees), byte-parity is a real cross-tree comparison (distinct inodes, empty branch<->master panel diff), the flush evicts the real module (id change), the real SynapsePanel is built (not the fallback). Two cosmetic notes (docstring scope overreach; sha_match near-tautological alone) were applied before the product commit.
